science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,212.9 K and log g 4.58 (u1 0.597, u2 0.166): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 6
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 7.04 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 6 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 2.4%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.32%, the light's own noise being 0.11%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. This campaign's three methods give its period (periodogram 7.01 d, wavelet 6.93 d, autocorrelation 7.13 d; periodogram peak 0.72), accepted by the criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43); the star's period is the mean of its 2 accepted campaigns. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 1 other star within 16 arcseconds, with under 0.1% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 6

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffe6d5, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 17 (March to May 2018): the map's scale, 96% to 104% of the mean surface, runs from a dark tone of the color to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 5.7% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · March to May 2018
